ratings.note: Freq: 11/100 reporters, only when length exceeds berth limit. Impact: screenshot shows a dead end with only a code and phone number; users restarted, retyped or phoned. Persistence: no in-flow recovery each time it occurs. s=4.

Freq: 7/100, 2/6 in usability. Impact: a wrong arrival time is booked and only discovered at the closed gate (waiting outside), safety-relevant but skippers' own tide knowledge often catches it. Persistence: no warning ever given. s=3.
Freq: 6/100; affects bowsprit boats. Impact: crop shows bare 'Length'; booked into a berth the boat does not fit, office must correct. Persistence: learned once known. s=3.

Freq: every booking reaches the page; new visitors (primary group) need the info; 2/6 usability. Impact: users phoned office or waited 40 min outside. Persistence: returning skippers learn the channel. s=3.

Freq: tide table is on the plan page used to pick arrival time; 8/100. Impact: screenshot shows UTC caption only; users arrived an hour off and met a closed gate. Persistence: once noticed, users convert. s=3.

Freq: 4/100, skippers who think in feet. Impact: crop shows 'Length' with no unit beside 'Draught in metres'; feet values lead to the BK-409 dead end or a wrong berth caught by the office. Persistence: learned after once. s=3.
Freq: every user comparing berths sees per-metre rates only (screenshot). Impact: mental arithmetic, annoyance, no error. Persistence: recurs each booking. s=2.

Freq: 5/100; headings differ across pages (screenshots show 'visitor berth' vs 'pontoon space'). Impact: doubt and extra checking, no failed bookings reported. Persistence: infrequent use means it recurs per visit. s=2.
Freq: 3/6 in usability stalled, 10/100 overall. Impact: crop shows bare 'MMSI' label with no hint; users stall or cannot proceed. Persistence: one-time once explained. s=3.
Freq: 5/94, boats without DSC radio (a small subset). Impact: required field blocks the critical booking task entirely; users phoned office. Persistence: never overcome online. s=4.
Freq: 7/100, only users who go Back. Impact: four fields emptied, retyped on a phone at sea; I rate 2 not 3 since the loss is short and re-enterable. Persistence: happens every Back. s=3.

Freq: 6/6 usability participants struggled; 15/100 reporters; core task. Impact: screenshot shows only an unlabelled '...' button; users restarted or said they would phone, some found it eventually. Persistence: learned once found. s=3.
Freq: all booking pages, all users. Impact: uncertainty about remaining steps on weak signal, no failures. Persistence: one-time; a short flow is learned. s=2.
